intro: A descendant, a capability, and the question of what actually supports it.

steps.caption: B descended from A. A had capability c. Does B's lineage establish that c depends on A?
Refused. A lineage edge generates a candidate support set and establishes none: c may have been copied into weights, recompiled, or rediscovered while the edge stayed.
steps.takeaway: Provenance is not causal support. Descent is not dependence.

actions.reason: REFUSED · support evidence of kind: provenance

steps.caption: Ablation: remove the support set under test and watch whether c survives. That is evidence of the kind the engine accepts.
Admitted: a continuity kernel K — a minimal, causally established support set for c under a declared replacement contract.
steps.takeaway: Support is set-shaped: K₁={A} and K₂={B,C} can both suffice, so deleting A alone proves nothing.

steps.caption: The engine has 4 capabilities, all synthetic, 0 observed. Both refusals fire; no kernel is claimed. Heredity is specified and unwitnessed, and this page says so.
steps.takeaway: Never write heredity in the present perfect: the engine runs and has nothing to run on.
